# Draft:Visits to 10 Downing Street by monarchs of the United Kingdom

On special occasions, monarchs of the United Kingdom have visited 10 Downing Street, long the official residence of the prime minister.
George V
1931 visit amid government crisis, aiming to aid in facilitation of the formation of a National Cabinet.
Edward VIII
Edward VII, during his short reign, privately came to the residence in an unsuccessful effort to lobby for Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin's support for the king's intents to marry Wallis Simpson
George VI
George VI somewhat frequently visited the residence as monarch.
3 September 1939 visit to residence during premiership of Neville Chamberlain.
Despite air raid risks, the king attended dinners with Prime Minister Churchill at the address during World War II.
Elizabeth II
*1985: Elizabeth attended a formal dinner held by Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher in the State Dinning Room  of 10 Downing to commemorate the 250th anniversary of George Downing taking residence at the address. The dinner was also attended by former prime ministers James Callaghan, Alec Douglas-Home, Harold Macmillan, Harold Wilson, and Edward Heath.
*April 2002: Elizabeth and Prince Phillip attended the Golden Jubilee Dinner hosted by Prime Minister Tony Blair and his wife, Cherie, in celebration of Elizabeth's Golden Jubilee as monarch. Former prime ministers Edward Heath, James Callaghan, Margaret Thatcher and John Major all attended the dinner.
*21 June 2011: Elizabeth and Prince Phillip attended a lunch hosted by Prime Minister David Cameron and his wife, Samantha Cameron, in celebration of Elizabeth's 90th birthday.
*24 July 2012: Elizabeth attended a lunch hosted by Prime Minister Cameron to commemorate her Diamond Jubilee. All living former British prime ministers had been invited, and Thatcher was the only who did not attend.  https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2012/jul/24/queen-lunch-downing-street-prime-ministers
*18 December 2012: to mark her diamond jubilee as monarch, Elizabeth attended a cabinet meeting at 10 Downing, which was the first cabinet meeting she had attended as monarch. https://www.upi.com/News_Photos/view/upi/67211c8b7fd83b04ed62a8ddb8242be2/Queen-Visits-No10-Downing-Street-for-Cabinet-Meting/  This marked a rare event,  https://www.theguardian.com/uk/gallery/2012/dec/18/queen-visits-downing-street-pictures as the last monarch to attend a cabinet meeting is believed to have been George III in 1781 https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-20757376.amp
